label: late original-phase steps of k-initial sequences, strongest on input t (weak, conjunctive)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.03% of steps). It fires only on the last few original-phase steps (orig_idx 4-8, most often 1-2 tokens before <DEL>) and weakly on the <DEL> step. It never fires in the copy phase or at t<4. Activation is enriched when the first token is k (67% of mass), when the input is t (55% of mass), and when the previous token is j or h. The largest activations combine all of these, e.g. k l 2 z h j [t]. None of these conditions alone or combined gives a coherent predicate: k-initial+late gives F1 0.07, t+late gives F1 0.05, and the best conjunction (late, input t, first token k) gives dev P 0.37, R 0.18, F1 0.25, with many misses on other late tokens in k-sequences. It looks like a hash-like conjunction of prefix identity and the current token.
